The statement reflects solid real-side momentum and ongoing disinflation, with policy held at a restrictive 5.25–5.50% and QT continuing until the Committee gains greater confidence on a sustainable move to 2% inflation. The Financial Stability Report tempers this otherwise constructive macro read: it highlights persistent vulnerabilities—elevated interest rate volatility and term premia, stress in commercial real estate (notably office vacancies and refinancing risk), tight risk premia relative to fundamentals in corporate credit (large triple‑B share and rising default metrics), leveraged hedge fund activity in Treasury futures that could amplify shocks, and structural vulnerabilities in money market funds—alongside concerns about public debt and global risks (including China). These stability risks argue for a cautious posture even as risks to the dual mandate move into better balance, reinforcing the Fed’s “higher for longer until confident” stance and readiness to adjust if market stress emerges.
